take_homes: The model fills gaps with plausible filler and grades its own work too kindly, so I check its claims against what I know.
What I learn can be saved as a text file the next session reads. That is different from a slide.
A fresh agent with no context can serve as a cold second reader.

monday.move: Take one real document of mine, have the agent critique it with a cold reader, and check whether its generic-line picks match my gut
monday.when: Tuesday, a 30-minute slot, if the first demo still seems worth it
monday.stop_condition: If the cold read is soft, generic or tells me nothing I didn't know, I stop
monday.blocker: Steering group calendar, and whether company data can go into the tool

misconception.why: They told me what doesn't work (self-grading is soft, filler is generic) and I could test it myself. That is not the agile slide. But half the module was the agile slide, and one toy exercise doesn't prove it won't blow over.

one_line: Strip out the 'note on context' filler and the look-back and rules-file parts are the first honest thing I've seen in one of these programmes. The rest is last year's slides.
